newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Spain blocks deal for S.Africa to join ACP.
newsitem.headline: Spain blocks deal for S.Africa to join ACP.

text.p: Spain on Monday blocked a proposal outlining the terms by which South Africa could become a partial member of the African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) group linked to the European Union, diplomats said.

They said Spain's Abel Matutes told his fellow EU foreign ministers during a meeting in Brussels that Madrid wanted to see more progress on bilateral relations between the EU and Pretoria before approving South Africa's partial accession to the Lome Convention.
The convention outlines relations between the EU and the 70 ACP countries and offers lucrative trade and other benefits to the developing world bloc.

Spain is seeking commitments from Pretoria for a separate fisheries agreement with the EU and also had reservations over the effect of imports of South African wines and spirits on the 15-nation bloc's market.
Diplomats said they hoped Spain could be persuaded to relent in time for South Africa's Lome membership to be put to the biennial EU/ACP meeting in Luxembourg in April.

In a statement, the foreign ministers said they would now consider "to what extent it will be possible to tke advantage of a facilitating clause...which would allow an early accession of South Africa to this convention without further ratification".
The EU has been wary of seeing South Africa become a full member for fear Pretoria's exports will prove superior in quantity and quality and swamp those of the rest of the bloc.
The European Commission -- the EU's executive -- has instead been negotiating partial membership that would exclude South African trade but alow Pretoria full political representation.
South Africa would aso be eligible for European Development Fund preferential loans.
EU foreign ministers did, however, approve a timetable for further negotiations on bilateral trade relations.

With an eye on the richest economy in sub-Saharan Africa, the EU wants a free trade deal excluding South African agricultural products, but Pretoria is seeking to include its farm products and is also wary of the effect any deal may have on its regional partners.
